title: Monthly 20% rainfall tails showed no clear spatial dependence difference across 48 US states in 1951-2025
abstract: We compared the spatial dependence of low and high monthly precipitation in 48 contiguous US states in 1951-2025. We used NOAA nClimDiv and local calendar-month 20% tails. Mean state-pair indicator correlation was 0.1166 for dry months and 0.1000 for wet months. The dry-minus-wet difference was 0.0166. Its 95% five-year block interval was -0.0007 to 0.0345 when each draw refit local thresholds. The primary test gives no clear difference. Results depend on the definition: 10% tails, strict inequalities and ten-year blocks gave positive intervals. The two separate 30-year periods and 30% tails gave intervals that include zero. We do not infer one stable national tail asymmetry. One gridded product, state boundaries, equal pair weights, rounded values and short-block uncertainty limit the result. Code, aggregate results, all bootstrap draws, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit are provided. Source records remain external.
